issues.problem: The new hand-wiring advice says a later block that sets 'options that change or leave out one of the pack's' makes the rule read overridden. The engine does not check that. judge() in src/lib/packs/standards.mjs only tests whether the manifest's `expect` subset holds: { mode: 'jsx-only' } for strings, { max } for size, plus the tag. The pack's other options are never compared: 'jsx-attributes': { exclude: NOT_TEXT } for strings, and skipBlankLines, skipComments and IIFEs for size. The test this commit adds is itself a counter-example. It drops skipComments and IIFEs from max-lines-per-function and replaces the pack's jsx-attributes exclude list with [], and it asserts both rules are measured. So the user-facing string, the standards guide and the setup skill each promise a check the code does not make. The commit message's 'the engine measures a rule whose effective options hold every one of the pack's' is also false.
issues.suggested_fix: Pick one and make the code and text agree. (a) Make the comparison cover every option the pack's export sets: derive each rule's `expect` from the export's own options (deep-equal per key the pack sets), so a dropped skipComments or a replaced jsx-attributes list reads overridden. Or (b) narrow the message, standards.md:23 and SKILL.md:164 to name only what is compared ('a severity other than error, a different mode or max limit, or a replaced tagged selector'), and say that other options a later block changes are not detected. Either way, rename and adjust the new standards.test.mjs case so it does not pin a changed jsx-attributes list as 'the pack's own options'.
issues.failure_scenario: An app spreads the pack's lines before its own block `{ files: ['**/*.tsx'], rules: { 'i18next/no-literal-string': ['error', { mode: 'jsx-only', 'jsx-attributes': { exclude: ['.*'] } }], 'max-lines-per-function': ['error', { max: 150 }] } }`. Following init's or doctor's advice, the developer expects these rules to read overridden, because the block changes jsx-attributes and leaves out skipBlankLines, skipComments and IIFEs. Instead doctor's lint row and the hook's standards line report expo strings and expo size as measured. Every JSX attribute string goes unflagged, and the size count includes blank lines and comments. The ratchet reports these numbers as the pack's rules when they are not.
issues.evidence: standards.mjs judge() (~line 108-114) only checks severity, the tag, and subset(want, options[0]), where want is the manifest's `expect` (e.g. mode or max). Other pack options (jsx-attributes exclude, skipBlankLines, skipComments, IIFEs) are never compared in wired(). The handAdd text at messages.mjs:~38-43, 'options that change or leave out one of the pack's ... reads overridden', therefore over-promises. Caveat: asSet() in scopeAt does compare all options exactly, but only for files covered by pack blocks and only where the later block applies. Doctor's wired lint row and the hook's standards line still report measured, and asSet() does not make the advice true.

issues.problem:
The list-item fence fix only knows an item's content indent when the fence is on the marker line itself. A fence on a continuation line of a nested item sits at 4 or more spaces (for example, after '- x' and '  - sub'). opens() rejects it because FENCE allows at most 3 leading spaces, so the block is never blanked. tableKeys() matches rows with line.trim().startsWith('|'), so a fenced example row inside it still counts as a documented entry. That contradicts 9ef8c4e's 'a table row inside a contract doc's fenced code block is not an entry' and the module header's 'outside a fenced code block (one a list item opens too)'. Measured: docKeys('- Example:
  - sub
    ```md
    | Fake | x |
    ```

## Real
') returns ['Fake', 'Real'].
issues.suggested_fix: Track the current list item's content indent across lines: set it from the last marker line and keep it while lines stay indented that far. Detect a fence relative to that indent (line.slice(indent) with 0-3 spaces), as within() already does for marker-line fences. Add the nested continuation case to entries.test.mjs. Or narrow the header comment and standards guide to fences on a top-level line or on a list marker line.

Button has no real entry. pack.expo.docs counts Button as documented, and the doctor row under-reports the undocumented primitives.
